title: Valuing the Billing Period Now Current on a Medicare Supplement Premium Account
content:
The premium owed for the billing period now current on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is fixed from what the premium account shows for that period.

**Where no charge stands for the billing period now current** — the period is valued at the monthly premium the household discount leaves, less the reduction, taken for each month the cadence covers.

**Where a charge stands for the billing period now current and a return has been paid against that period** — the period is valued at the amount posted less the amount returned.

**Where neither of those holds** — the period is valued at the amount posted for it.

### Input, judgement, outcome

> *Input.* The account shows no charge at all for the billing period now current. The monthly premium the household discount leaves is 114.71, the reduction is 2.00, and the cadence bills 3 months at a time.
> *Judgement.* No charge stands for the period.
> *Outcome.* The period is valued at 114.71 less 2.00, being 112.71, taken for each of the 3 months the cadence covers, giving 338.13.

> *Input.* The account shows a charge of 344.13 for the billing period now current, and a return of 114.71 paid against that period.
> *Judgement.* A charge stands and a return has been paid against the period.
> *Outcome.* The period is valued at 344.13 less 114.71, being 229.42.

> *Input.* The account shows a charge of 344.13 for the billing period now current and no return paid against it.
> *Judgement.* A charge stands and no return has been paid against the period.
> *Outcome.* The period is valued at the amount posted for it, being 344.13.

The first case is the only one in which the monthly premium is used at all; wherever a charge stands for the period, the amount posted is what the period is worth, whether or not a return has since been paid against it.
